key_insight: DeepQuest links knowledge gaps, data feasibility, and evidence auditing to generate traceable, testable hypotheses for Alzheimer's disease research.
engineering_relevance: Research-agent pipelines can assess experimental reliability separately from contribution to existing knowledge rather than treating successful execution as discovery.
method: Extract unresolved questions from domain reviews and convert them into traceable hypotheses.
Screen hypotheses for data feasibility and prioritize them using groupwise Elo ranking.
Run iterative experiments with two-level auditing against two frozen literature corpora.
evidence_signal: On OASIS-3, DeepQuest generated 42 feasible hypotheses, achieved a 95.24% audit-assessed scientific finding rate, and beat the strongest baselines in 14 of 15 evaluator-dimension comparisons; key associations were supported in ADNI and AIBL.
watch_item: The finding rate is audit-assessed against frozen literature corpora, so it should not be equated with prospective experimental confirmation or clinical validity.
paper_title: DeepQuest: From Knowledge Gaps to Scientific Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease
